stories.head: ChatGPT Ads vs. Google Ads: B2B Tests Show Comparable CPCs but Weaker Conversions
stories.plain: Early B2B tests place ChatGPT ad CPCs near Google's levels but show lower engagement, fewer conversions, and much less targeting control. This directly affects how marketers allocate paid budgets and whether AI-native ad surfaces can compete with search. Buyers and planners need a clear-eyed benchmark before shifting spend.

stories.head: Automation Anywhere Completes Boost.ai Acquisition to Build Autonomous Customer Service Platform
stories.plain: Automation Anywhere has closed its purchase of Boost.ai, combining enterprise conversational and voice AI with agentic process automation. The combined platform targets regulated industries where agents must both talk to customers and trigger backend actions. This consolidation reshapes the competitive map for autonomous customer service and pressures legacy SaaS CX vendors.

stories.head: AI Agents Now Initiate 13% of Website Visits, Attentive MCP Reaches Snowflake
stories.plain: A Cequence study finds AI agents account for 13% of web visits, signalling a structural shift in traffic composition that breaks classic analytics assumptions. Separately, Attentive's MCP connector reaching Snowflake means messaging decisions can draw directly on warehouse data — a meaningful step for real-time personalisation at scale.

stories.head: Atypica CPO Angela Xu on When — and When Not — to Trust AI-Generated Customer Personas
stories.plain: Atypica's CPO explains how synthetic AI personas can close the survey say-do gap but warns of specific failure modes practitioners must check. As more teams replace qual research with AI-generated audiences, understanding where synthetic data misleads is a core governance skill for anyone buying or building marketing AI.

stories.head: FalkorDB Brings Graph Database and GraphRAG to Valkey Open-Source Infrastructure
stories.plain: FalkorDB's new module lets teams run graph queries and GraphRAG retrieval inside the Valkey datastore they already operate, lowering the infrastructure cost of building AI agents that reason across connected customer and product data. This matters for anyone architecting agentic marketing systems that need fast, relationship-aware context.

stories.head: ChatGPT Ads vs. Google Ads: B2B performance data compared
stories.plain: Early B2B tests show ChatGPT ads match Google on cost-per-click but trail badly on engagement, conversions, and targeting control. This matters because it gives buyers the first real performance benchmark for AI-native ad inventory — a signal that shapes where marketing budgets flow and how GEO strategy should be prioritised.

stories.head: Six questions to vet real AI from relabelled automation in martech RFPs
stories.plain: A practical buying guide that gives procurement and marketing ops teams six diagnostic questions to separate genuine AI capability from old-rule automation with an AI badge. This directly changes how platforms are evaluated and bought — cutting through vendor hype at the moment a contract decision is made.

stories.head: Automation Anywhere completes Boost.ai acquisition to unify conversational AI with agentic automation
stories.plain: Automation Anywhere has closed its purchase of Boost.ai, combining enterprise conversational and voice AI with agentic process automation for regulated industries. The merger creates a platform that can take a customer conversation all the way to a completed back-office action — a structural shift in how autonomous customer service is built and sold.

stories.head: What's missing from your 2027 marketing AI budget
stories.plain: The piece argues that most marketing AI budgets fund tools but skip the people, training, and change-management costs that determine whether those tools actually work. With 2027 budget cycles opening now, this framing directly influences how organisations plan and govern AI spending — not just what they buy.

stories.head: adMarketplace full-year data: AI search ad conversions up 156% but behaviour varies by platform
stories.plain: A full year of live data from adMarketplace's AI Discovery product shows conversion rates 156% higher than standard search ads, but purchase intent and product interest shift significantly across browsers, comparison engines, and BNPL apps. The finding matters because it proves AI search surfaces cannot be treated as one channel when planning or buying media.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Reshaping the Purchase Funnel from Both Ends
body: AI agents are now acting as autonomous buyers on behalf of enterprise customers — evaluating B2B vendors, filtering search results, and sitting inside collaboration tools like Slack and Google Chat. This means brands must optimize not just for human readers but for machine-readable credibility signals that agents use to shortlist vendors.

At the same time, personal AI agents are being deployed for end consumers, compressing the discovery-to-decision journey. Marketing ops teams that treat AI-agent readiness as a back-burner project risk becoming invisible before a human buyer ever enters the picture.

themes.head: The AI Creative Risk Reckoning Arrives
body: Automated creative generation is moving faster than the guardrails around it. Brand, legal, and regulatory exposure from auto-generated assets is no longer theoretical — from copyright ambiguity to regulatory non-compliance, the liability lands with the marketer, not the model vendor.

Enterprise AI governance frameworks are being stress-tested and found wanting: a governance policy alone cannot protect a brand when the output pipeline runs at machine speed. Human review checkpoints and business-context grounding are emerging as non-negotiable requirements, not optional upgrades.
ev: MarTech · Hidden risks of auto-generated creative
MarTech · AI needs your business knowledge

themes.head: ChatGPT Ads vs. Google: A New Media Buying Decision
body: OpenAI's move into advertising creates a genuine fork in paid media strategy. ChatGPT ads operate inside a conversational, intent-rich context that differs structurally from keyword auctions — engagement patterns, attribution logic, and creative formats are all distinct, requiring separate evaluation rather than a simple budget reallocation.

Data from adMarketplace reinforces the point: consumers behave differently across AI search experiences, meaning a single creative and bidding approach will underperform across both surfaces. Marketers now need a framework for deciding which queries, audiences, and funnel stages belong on which platform.
ev: MarTech · ChatGPT ads vs. Google Ads
Agile Brand · AI search advertising engagement data

themes.head: AI Budget & Stack Decisions Demand Rigorous New Criteria
body: Planning cycles for 2027 are exposing a gap: most AI line items were added reactively and lack success metrics, ownership, or sunset criteria. What's missing isn't money — it's a decision framework for evaluating which AI capabilities actually compound returns versus which create technical debt.

RFP processes are catching up, with new guidance on how to vet AI claims during vendor selection. Mid-market teams in particular are finding that AI is restructuring role boundaries, not just automating tasks, which makes headcount and tooling decisions inseparable.

themes.head: Synthetic Personas & AI-Powered Customer Understanding Go Mainstream
body: AI-generated customer personas — built from behavioral data and psychological models rather than survey panels — are moving from experiment to operational tool. The critical new question isn't whether to use them, but when to trust a synthetic customer signal over a real one, especially for edge cases and emerging segments.

Psychology-informed design of AI personas is gaining traction as a corrective to flat, demographic-only models. Richer mental models of customer motivation improve personalization accuracy and reduce the risk of AI recommendations that are statistically plausible but contextually wrong.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — creative, media, personas, agents, and budgets — AI is forcing marketers to make structural decisions they can no longer defer to a future planning cycle.
